meta.title: Task complete notice
meta.description: Shows a notice in the top-right corner of the window and plays a chime whenever the agent of a session stops running, or starts waiting for you to answer a question, review a plan, or approve an action. A finished run reads as finished, not as success: a normal completion, a failure, and the Stop button all trigger it. A waiting interaction stays on screen until it is answered, so a question asked while you were away is still there when you come back. Click a notice to open that session, or close it with the cross. Up to three notices stack. Finished notices leave after about seven seconds of your attention: their countdown holds while the window is unfocused, the page is hidden, or you hover or focus the notice. Only listed top-level sessions are observed, so subagent runs stay silent. The notice is drawn inside the page and the chime is synthesised in the browser (a two-note chime for a stop, a longer three-note one for a waiting interaction), so it works only while a Harness web or desktop window is open and sends no system notification. Timing, stack size, and chime volume are constants at the top of client.js.
